messages.subject: colour scheme
parts:
I make this graphic:
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3180464/testcolors.jpeg

with this code:
qplot(data=AlfootpLm,x=wl,y=Reflectance,geom=c("point","path"),group=date,colour=doy)
+ facet_grid(year ~ season)+scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(1,365))

Data:
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3180464/AlfootpLm.rda

The problem is that the colors have a very low contrast. I've tried
qplot(data=AlfootpLm,x=wl,y=Reflectance,geom=c("point","path"),group=date,colour=doy)
+ facet_grid(year ~
season)+scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(1,365),low="blue",high="red")

but the contrast is still very low. I think that the problem is that
the default color scheme is not appropriate
(please correct me in case I'm wrong). How do I actually
change the color scheme to, for example, a rainbow? Is there a list of
alternative color schemes?

Thanks

Agus

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: colour scheme
parts:
Baptiste has started a 3 part series on color on the ggplot2 blog that you should probably look at. It's a pretty good introduction to using colors in ggplot2. 

http://blog.ggplot2.org/

I found a low and high that I liked and thought separated the data a bit better. 

qplot(data=AlfootpLm,x=wl,y=Reflectance,geom=c("point","path"),group=date,colour=doy)+ facet_grid(year ~ season)+ scale_colour_gradient(low="Purple", high="Yellow")

It's completely relative though. You kind of have to find what you like and what will communicate what you want to your audience most effectively.

Agus

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: colour scheme
parts:
Agus, 

The "colors=" option in continuous_scale is not documented (although we should fix that). 

I do not know how to display all of the options for the colors, but perhaps someone else will. 

You can play with the breaks to get the yellow color to appear...

qplot(data=AlfootpLm,x=wl,y=Reflectance,geom=c("point","path"),group=date,colour=doy)+facet_grid(year~season)+scale_colour_gradientn(limits=c(1,365),colours=rainbow(365), breaks=c(1, seq(30, 360, 30)))

I'm pretty sure that brewer scales are always discrete so giving them to a continuous scale will never work. 

Salu2,

 B

This is a very good solution:

qplot(data=AlfootpLm,x=wl*1000,y=Reflectance/10,geom=c("point","path"),group=date,colour=doy,
xlab="Wavelength (nm)", ylab="Reflectance (%)") + facet_grid(year ~
season) + scale_colour_gradientn(limits=c(1,365),colours=rainbow(365),breaks=c(1,seq(60,365,by=60)),"DoY")
